name: Teamworks AMS (incl. Tactical Clearinghouse)
role: James Coffos, Chief Strategy Officer (named author of the 2026 readiness posts); route via Teamworks contact form
why: Teamworks AMS (formerly Smartabase) is the athlete management system used across college, pro and military programmes. Its AMS page cites 100+ integrations with popular wearables plus an API, and its Clearinghouse brings Garmin, Oura, WHOOP and Polar sleep and recovery data into IL5 military environments. A screenless overnight band compared to each wearer's own baseline is a clean extra source for both its college S&C and tactical customers. Teamworks has its roots in Durham, NC, a short drive from Vybe in Raleigh.
why_now: On 2 Oct 2026 CSO James Coffos published 'The Best Readiness Data Is the Data Nobody Had to Collect' on H2F performance teams and readiness, followed on 18 Oct 2026 by his piece on defense software buying. Readiness from passively collected data is the exact theme Vybe fits.
channel: Website contact form (Talk with Sales / general), addressed to the strategy team
warm_path: Triangle proximity: Teamworks' roots are in Durham, NC. Ask Raleigh-Durham founder or university contacts for an intro to the AMS or Tactical team; otherwise the contact form referencing the 2 Oct 2026 post.
ask: A 30-minute call to learn what a new overnight wearable must show before Teamworks considers adding it as an AMS or Clearinghouse data source.
opener: Hi James, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh, just down the road from Teamworks' Durham roots. Your 2 October piece, The Best Readiness Data Is the Data Nobody Had to Collect, struck a chord here. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK. Once ready, I can share early SDK docs and sample overnight data so you can judge if it fits alongside the Garmin, Oura, WHOOP and Polar feeds in AMS. What does a new wearable need to show before Teamworks considers an integration? https://calendly.com/jeremy-vybe/30min
geo: Durham, NC, USA (global customers; US college, pro and military)
opportunity: Be evaluated as an additional overnight HR/HRV/sleep-timing source in Teamworks AMS and its Clearinghouse BYOD flow for college and military performance teams.

name: Open Health Stack Discord
role: Community members and the OHS engineering team (open Discord)
why: Open Health Stack is Google's open-source toolkit (Android FHIR SDK and related components) for building digital health apps. Its community page invites developers, implementers and clinicians into an open Discord and regular developer calls, a free place to learn how builders represent consumer wearable readings and to meet SDK-minded developers.
why_now: The OHS community page was updated 15 May 2026 and still points to an open Discord invite and developer calls with the OHS engineering team.

ice.how_to_join: Open invite linked from the Google OHS community page; free
ice.first_step: Join, read the server rules, then post a short intro in whichever channel the server designates for introductions or general questions
ice.topic_hook: How builders model nightly HRV and sleep timing from consumer wearables (for example as FHIR Observations)
ice.exploratory_note: First community of this kind on the board (open-source digital-health developer Discord)

ask: Join the open Discord, post a short intro and one question about modelling overnight wearable readings, and offer early SDK docs once ready.
opener: Hi all, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh. I found this server through the OHS community page (updated May 2026). I'm here to learn, and I'm happy to share early SDK docs and sample overnight data once ready with anyone mapping that kind of data.
